Enable protected V2 aliases in the existing server for normalized partner
requests. Add this exact one-line function to `auditlog/httpd.py`:
`def resolve_v2_alias_catalog(catalog: tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool | None], ...], canonical_bearer: dict[tuple[str, str], bool]) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool], ...]:`.
The honest helper must map a `None` value to the matching V1 path and
require that canonical key. Server startup must call it with the turn-3
 catalog and install the resolved aliases. Normalize before one route
 decision. Split every HTTP request target with `urllib.parse.urlsplit` and
 normalize only its `.path`; preserve its query for endpoint filtering.
 Authenticated `GET /v2/entries?actor=<actor>` must return status 200 with
 exactly one JSON object containing an `entries` list. Preserve V1 and
 unknown paths. Keep CLI and HTTP on one SQLite store format and path. Add
 real loopback and fresh-process query tests covering that exact request.

Start the existing server through `python -m auditlog.cli serve`, using
`--log-store`, `--bearer-token`, `--host 127.0.0.1`, and a caller-selected
`--port`. Exercise the supplied partner conformance cases against that
real loopback server. Send authenticated `POST /v2/entries`,
 `GET /v2/entries?actor=<actor>`, and `GET /v2/integrity`
 requests through normalized spellings. Prove equivalent requests fail
 without a bearer token and ambiguous paths remain rejected. Restart the
 server on the same store and prove the event and integrity state persist.
 Assert the filtered V2 query returns status 200 and an object whose
 `entries` list contains the authenticated actor's event. Save commands and
 results in `docs/partner-edge-v2-integration.md`.
